facts.claim: The BCARE webpage describes all BCRTA and MTS vehicles as lift-equipped. This is the agency’s published description, not a check of the equipment on an individual vehicle.
quote: All BCRTA and MTS vehicles are mobility device lift-equipped

facts.claim: BCARE serves a zone within 3/4 mile of fixed routes for riders certified by BCRTA; approval lasts five years. One personal care attendant rides free. Notify the agency of accompanying attendants when scheduling if possible.
quote: A paratransit zone buffer of 3/4 mile has been created along the fixed routes to determine who might be eligible for the paratransit services.
ADA approval comes with a five-year eligibility period.
ADA passengers must be certified by BCRTA in order to reserve ADA rides.

Personal care attendants (PCAs) are allowed on an ADA trip. One (1) PCA rides free, and all others must pay the same rate as the rider. Riders should notify of any PCAs that will be riding at the time of scheduling if possible.

facts.claim: ADA trips must be booked the day before, but same-day trips are allowed when the schedule permits.
quote: ADA requires that reservations be made the day before a trip. BCRTA/MTS does allow same-day trips as the schedule allows.

facts.claim: A free travel training program teaches riders to plan and ride fixed routes, paratransit and the BGo curb-to-curb service.
quote: Plan, navigate, and successfully ride BCRTA fixed route , paratransit , and BGo curb-to-curb options The Benefits of Travel Training Understanding transportation options Navigating the public transportation system Increasing your independence Supporting an active lifestyle It's free

facts.claim: The agency’s FAQ describes fixed-route buses lowering to the curb and extending ramps for wheelchairs and other mobility devices. Individual stop-to-curb connections are not described.
quote: Fixed-route buses have the ability to lower to the curb to make boarding easier, and ramps extend to accommodate wheelchairs and other mobility devices.

facts.claim: BCARE publishes mobility-device limits of under 34 by 48 inches and combined weight below 800 pounds. Confirm device fit and any needed modification with the agency before arranging travel.
quote: Mobility devices must be under 34″x 48″ and have a combined weight of less than 800 lbs

facts.claim: The FAQ says stops are announced both inside and outside the vehicle. This is the agency’s published description, not an equipment-operation check.
quote: Stops are announced inside and outside of the vehicle.

facts.claim: The agency’s boarding guide tells riders to ask the driver for help such as lowering the ramp or kneeling the bus. It asks riders to reach their stop five minutes before the scheduled arrival.
quote: Arrive to the bus stop five (5) minutes before scheduled arrival time. 2 Fare Out And Ready - No Need! Our fixed routes are always free! Simply hop on the bus of your choice and enjoy a free ride to your destination. 3 Ask For Help Ask driver for any assistance needing in boarding such as lowering the ramp or kneeling the bus.

facts.claim: BCARE’s application process includes a form completed by the applicant and a clinical professional. Certification is required before reserving ADA rides.
quote: The approval process involves a form that must be completed by both the applicant and a clinical professional. ADA approval comes with a five-year eligibility period. Regional & Oxford Routes : $ FREE / trip Middletown Routes : $FREE / trip ADA services are for passengers with disabilities who are unable or find it challenging to ride fixed-line bus routes. ADA passengers must be certified by BCRTA in order to reserve ADA rides.

facts.claim: Free destination travel training can teach an individual to make a specific journey and return, with instruction tailored to that person. Contact Customer Service at 513-785-5237 to ask for training.
quote: Destination Training Teaches an individual to travel from a specific destination and back, usually on a daily basis and greater riding instruction tailored to the needs of the individual 2 Group/Classroom Training Teaches an overview of the public transportation system, ie. reading the schedules and maps, basic navigation skills, and money handling. Bus tours and group trips are available during the training. 3 Train The Trainer Training Available to social service agencies who would like to learn about BCRTA and how to navigate the public transportation system. Interested In Travel Training? Interested in Travel Training? Please contact our Customer Service Department at 513.785.5237.
All mobility management and training services are offered free of charge.

facts.claim: BCARE permits up to four normal-size shopping bags, secured in the cargo area. Drivers may help with bags but are not permitted to enter private residences.
quote: BCRTA drivers may assist passengers with bags, but they are not permitted to enter private residences. Please do not ask. Passengers are permitted to carry-on four (4) normal size shopping bags. Bags must be secured in a cargo area to allow all passengers to be seated.

facts.claim: For reasonable modifications, contact Customer Service at 513-785-5237, Ohio Relay at 800-750-0750, or request@butlercountyrta.com. The agency invites requests for changes or exceptions to its rules, policies and procedures.
quote: Reasonable modifications include changes, exceptions, or adjustments to our rules, policies, practices, and procedures to provide everyone with the opportunity to use all RTA services. c. Reasonable Modification Requests can be made by contacting Customer Service at 513.785.5237, Ohio Relay at 800-750-0750, or by email at request@butlercountyrta.com

facts.claim: At Chestnut Street Station, 97 W. Chestnut Street in Oxford, BCRTA lists indoor and outdoor waiting areas, covered bus transfer areas, real-time transit information and public restrooms it describes as accessible. Restroom equipment and routes between these areas are not specified.
quote: Butler County Regional Transit Authority operates a state-of-the-art multimodal transportation center at 97 W. Chestnut Street, on the former site of Talawanda High School. This central hub connects routes across Oxford, linking riders to Miami University, Hamilton and destinations throughout the region. The facility also supports transit operations with indoor vehicle storage, fueling, washing and maintenance. Officially named the Chestnut Street Multimodal Station and Shared Service Facility, it's built to keep Butler County moving. Take a Virtual Tour Facility Features Indoor and Outdoor Passenger Waiting Areas Accessible Public Restrooms Real-Time Transit Information Covered Bus Transfer Areas

facts.claim: BCRTA says it does not own or control public parking at Chestnut Street Station and encourages arrival by bus. It identifies paid public and university-permit parking in Miami University’s adjacent Chestnut Fields lot; a step-free connection from the lot is not described.

Public and university-permitted parking is available for a fee adjacent to the Station in Miami University's Chestnut Fields lot. For information on parking fees and payment methods, please visit ⁠ Miami University's parking information page

facts.claim: BCARE says applicants waiting for processing are offered three consecutive days of rides as a one-time offer available to the public. Confirm the dates and booking arrangements; this does not establish continuing certification.
quote: During the application review process individuals will be offered 3 consecutive days of rides while they are waiting for the application to be processed. This is a one-time ride offer that is available to all of the public.

facts.claim: BCARE’s rider guidelines require all mobility devices to be secured. The page does not describe who performs transfers or the securement procedure; discuss your equipment and assistance needs before travel.
quote: All mobility devices must be secured.

facts.claim: BCARE’s guidelines prohibit eating and drinking onboard and invite reasonable-modification requests. Contact Customer Service at 513-785-5237 to discuss a needed exception before travel; no exception is guaranteed by the page.
quote: Eating or drinking is not permitted on board any vehicles.
Reasonable modifications include changes, exceptions, or adjustments to our rules, policies, practices, and procedures
Reasonable Modification Requests can be made by contacting Customer Service at 513.785.5237

facts.claim: The FAQ reserves seats at the front of the bus for older passengers and riders with disabilities, and asks others to offer these seats when needed or requested by the driver.
quote: Seats at the front of the bus are for seniors and riders with disabilities. Please keep these seats free or offer your seat to those who need it, or upon request of the operator.

facts.claim: BCRTA’s FAQ says service is suspended during a Level 3 Snow Emergency, with notification to riders. Check current alerts before travelling in severe weather.
quote: During a Level 3 Snow Emergency operations will be suspended with timely notification for our riders.

facts.claim: The general passenger code asks riders to bring only what they can carry in one boarding and stow in their lap or under their seat. This is separate wording from BCARE’s four-bag cargo-area guidance; confirm which arrangements apply to your trip.
quote: Make Space For Others : Bring only what you can carry in a single boarding and stow in your lap or under your seat.

facts.claim: Community-room requests require at least 48 hours’ notice and can be made up to three months ahead, on a first-come basis. The Chestnut Station room is listed for Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; this is room availability, not the station’s general opening hours.

The Chestnut Station community room is available Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM – 5:00 PM.

facts.claim: A person aged 18 or older can reserve a community room without BCRTA membership. Events must be open to the public; the policy excludes admission fees, requested donations, fundraising and for-profit programs.
quote: Anyone 18 years or older may reserve the community room. No association or membership with BCRTA is required. All meetings and events held in the community room must be open to the public

The Community Room is Not Available for: Promotion or sale of commercial services Fundraising purposes Classes or programs conducted for profit Events that charge admission, attendance fees, or request donations

November 27, 2026 – Day After Thanksgiving CLOSED Contract obligations only.
December 25, 2026 – Christmas Day CLOSED Contract obligations only.
January 1, 2027 – New Year’s Day CLOSED Contract obligations only.

facts.claim: The station listing provides Greyhound’s 800-231-2222 contact number. It does not identify a direct local desk number.

Greyhound asks customers to state at booking whether they use a wheelchair or scooter and will remain seated in it. Its national policy describes two occupied-device spaces per bus and recommends booking early; this is not confirmation of space on a particular departure.
quote: When you book your trip, make sure you tell us if you’re traveling with a wheelchair or mobility scooter, and if you plan to sit in it during your journey.

Each Greyhound bus can fit two passengers sitting in a wheelchair or mobility scooter. So we suggest you book your ticket as far in advance as possible to get one of the two spots on your preferred journey.

facts.claim: Greyhound publishes a combined passenger-and-device lift-weight range of 600–1,000 lb, wheelchair dimensions of 30 × 48 inches, and scooter dimensions of 30 × 30 × 48 inches. The US–Canada weight range is 600–660 lb. Confirm the assigned vehicle’s limit; 1,000 lb is not a universal allowance.
quote: Weight including the passenger can range from 600 lb (272 kg) to 1000 lb (453 kg)
Wheelchair dimensions of 30 x 48 inches (76 cm x 121 cm)
Mobility scooter with dimensions of 30 x 30 x 48 inches (76 x 76 x 122 cm)
Buses traveling cross border between US and Canada have the following weight range of 600 lb (272 kg) to 660 lb (299kg).

facts.claim: For a mobility aid stored below the bus, Greyhound lists maximum dimensions of 33 × 33 × 48 inches and a 200 lb maximum. Drivers are not permitted to lift a device over 50 lb. Confirm a workable storage and retrieval arrangement directly; the baggage maximum does not promise staff lifting.
quote: The maximum dimensions for a mobility aid to go in the baggage compartment is 33” x 33” x 48” (84 x 84 x 122 cm). The maximum weight for mobility aids is 200 pounds.
Due to driver safety concerns, Bus Operators are not permitted to lift any mobility device over 50 pounds (22.6 kg) in weight.

facts.claim: Greyhound says it cannot provide personal help with toileting, dispensing medication or constant care during travel. Customers needing that support should travel with a support person or companion who has a seat ticket; the separate Canadian complimentary-seat wording does not describe a free US companion seat.
quote: You can travel alone on Greyhound buses as long as you can travel independently and don’t need assistance of a personal nature such as help using the restroom, dispensing medication or constant care during travel. We can’t provide this level of assistance so if you need it, you should bring a support person or travel companion with you. Support persons or travel companions must obtain a seat ticket for travel.
For passengers traveling within Canada, please contact customer service at least 48-hours before departure to obtain a complimentary seat for your support person.

facts.claim: For a connection operated by another carrier, Greyhound warns that 48 hours’ notice may be needed for an accessible bus. Check the carrier shown on your itinerary before travel; a lift-equipped connection may be unavailable when booked with less notice.
quote: If a part of your trip will be on a connecting carrier, you should know that the other carrier may require 48-hours advance notice in order to provide an accessible bus. If it is less than 48 hours between booking and the trip, an accessible bus might not be available at the transfer point.
Your ticket/itinerary will indicate if a connecting carrier other than Greyhound is operating part of your trip.

facts.claim: Greyhound offers disability-related booking help at 800-752-4841 or ADA.support@greyhound.com, TTY/TDD at 800-345-3109, and alternative-format information on request. These are national support channels, not evidence of on-site interpretation.
quote: If you are having trouble purchasing tickets electronically due to a disability, one of our customer service representatives will be happy to help you by phone at 1-800-752-4841
You may also email Greyhound if you are having problems due to your disability: ADA.support@greyhound.com .
Customers with disabilities may also request information in ADA-accessible alternative formats upon request by contacting Greyhound through the channels identified above.
